jobs.prompt:
This is goal g-33a7a4ae, round 2 (fix round; round 1 was audit-only and already merged as docs/state/silent-failures.md; several fix batches already merged for other files). Read that doc's methodology section first (top of file) and the per-file section for tools/gpu.mjs (search for '### tools/gpu.mjs' - it lists exact line numbers, all try-catch-no-binding).

IMPORTANT - this file is sensitive (MONEY): it manages real hourly-billed rented GPU nodes over ssh. Three flagged catches (re-find by content, not by exact line number) swallow a failed remote stop-servers/stop-tunnel call: `afterStartFailure`'s ssh stop attempt (comment: 'ignored: the timer still removes them'), its matching stopTunnel attempt ('already gone'), and the main stop path's stopTunnel attempt ('already gone'). These already have a real safety net (a dead-man timer on the rented node that powers it off at the session's expiry regardless), so the existing silent-and-continue behavior is genuinely safe by design - do NOT add a throw or change what happens next. But a failed remote stop still means the node keeps running (and billing) until that timer fires, which could be a real delay - so these three deserve a real log (case b: unconditional, no narrowing) so an operator can see 'the stop call failed, relying on the dead-man timer' rather than it vanishing entirely.

The other three flagged catches are ordinary best-effort/expected-during-normal-operation cases: `removeSession`'s file cleanup (the session file may already be gone), a replica-starting poll loop ('still starting, or not JSON yet' - fetch to a server that isn't up yet), and a replica health check ('down' - fetch to an unreachable/stopped replica). Treat these per the normal rules below.

For EACH flagged line in tools/gpu.mjs only (do not touch any other file, do not fix findings in other files even if you notice them while reading):

1. Read the surrounding function to understand what the catch is actually guarding against and what happens today when it swallows silently (what does the function return/do next).
2. Decide, from the real code, whether this catch is:
   (a) An EXPECTED/benign condition - the file-cleanup, starting-poll, and health-check sites described above. For these, keep the swallow (do not change control flow or add noisy logging for the expected path), narrow to a specific error/network code only where one clearly applies, and add minimal visibility (see point 3) for anything else unexpected - same return value, same behavior, just visible.
   (b) The three dead-man-timer-backed stop/cleanup catches described above, or any other genuinely unexpected case. Add minimal visibility only: a one-line log. This file has no existing logger/journal convention of its own for these catches - use `console.error('[tools/gpu.mjs] <short context naming the function/operation>:', error?.message ?? error)`. Do NOT add a throw, do NOT change the function's return value or control flow, do NOT change what happens next.
3. If a catch binds no error variable, add a REAL binding and actually reference it in a console.error call - do not just rename-and-ignore a binding.

Do not refactor anything beyond the flagged catch blocks. Do not reformat unrelated code. Do not rename functions or change exports. Preserve every existing behavior path exactly except for the narrowing/visibility described above - the dead-man timer remains the only enforced guarantee, these catches must never themselves become a blocking or throwing path.

Your workspace does not include the test suite, so you cannot run it yourself - the orchestrator runs the real full suite against your output after integration, and will also get this reviewed via the claude CLI before merge given the sensitivity (money/GPU billing), and will send back any issue as a follow-up. List, in your final summary, which of the 6 flagged lines you touched, how (unconditional log for the three stop/cleanup sites, or case a/b for the rest), with one line each.
